title: Monotonicity of the recorded run radius
statement: Let a run of a $K$-work-tape machine $R$ on input $x$ start at configuration $a$, end at configuration $b$ after $t$ steps, and avoid the states $\mathrm{yes}$ and $\mathrm{no}$ at every time $u<t$. Suppose also that, at every time $u\le t$ and on every tape $j$, the distance between the work-head position and a specified base position is at most $r$. For any natural number $r'\ge r$, these same run and state-avoidance conditions hold, and all those distances are at most $r'$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $K$, symbol type $\Gamma$, and state type $S$
A $K$-work-tape machine $R$ and distinguished states $\mathrm{yes},\mathrm{no}\in S$
A base position for each of the $K$ tapes
Configurations $a,b$ on input $x$ and a natural number $t$
At each time $u<t$, the state is neither $\mathrm{yes}$ nor $\mathrm{no}$
At each time $u\le t$ and on every tape, the absolute difference between its head position and base position is at most $r$
